title: Morning Brief — Fri 27 Nov

stories.board: Supreme Court rules today on Quebec's Bill 21
stories.headline: Canada's top court decides on Quebec's religious symbols law
stories.what: This morning the Supreme Court of Canada rules on Bill 21. That Quebec law stops some public workers, like teachers and police, from wearing religious symbols such as a kippah, hijab or turban at work.
stories.why: Quebec used the notwithstanding clause (a rule that lets a province override some Charter rights), and the ruling could change how all provinces may use it.
stories.sides: Quebec's premier and other provinces say the clause is a fair tool for elected lawmakers; rights groups and religious groups who sued say it hurts minorities' freedom.

stories.board: New Zealand election ends with no winner
stories.headline: New Zealand's final count gives no side a majority
stories.what: After counting all votes from the Nov 7 election, the right-leaning government has 65 seats and the left side 65 with a new small party, Opportunity. 66 seats are needed to rule.
stories.why: A tiny party now picks who leads, and a new government could take weeks.
stories.sides: No major disagreement on the count. Opportunity says it will talk to National first, but National's leader ruled that out during the campaign.

stories.board: World stocks jump as Wall Street reopens
stories.headline: Stock markets rise around the world after Thanksgiving
stories.what: Markets in Asia and Europe went up, and US stock futures (early bets on today's prices) rose almost 2 percent. US markets open for a short day and close at 1 p.m.
stories.why: Buying in AI companies and help from China for its markets lifted prices, while oil stays high near 98 US dollars a barrel.
stories.sides: No major disagreement. AP notes worries about planned new US tariffs (taxes on imports) and tension in the Middle East.

quick_hits: Israel: Gadi Eisenkot signed a deal with Yair Golan's party and hopes to finish talks with Naftali Bennett by Saturday night, but his side is still short of 61 seats.
PM Carney goes to Yellowknife today to announce a big new plan to connect Canada's North.
Ukraine's President Zelensky warns Russia is planning another big missile attack in the coming days.
big_picture: Courts, voters and coalitions are deciding who holds power, in Canada, New Zealand and Israel.
